correctness.rationale: For C4 strictly convex positive-curvature-radius support functions and homogeneous Poisson normal angles, the exact tangent-leg identity gives area coefficient r²/24 and perimeter coefficient r/12 per cubic angular gap. Exact one- and two-point Palm identities for the cubic-gap functional give mean 6 lambda^-2 integral w and asymptotic cross-covariance 504 lambda^-5 integral wv (diagonal contribution 720 and two near-neighbor contributions -108 each). Truncation into independent Poisson blocks yields a Cramer–Wold Gaussian limit with negligible gap and geometric errors, and L2 error yields moment covariance convergence. Cauchy–Schwarz gives the determinant and its equality case; constant curvature radius solves h+h''=R and hence characterizes translated disks. Standard-library checker reconstructs genuine tangent polygons for circle and perturbed circle, verifies exact circle area–perimeter dependence and approximate covariance scaling. Finite simulations are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The new theorem concerns exact supporting tangent halfplanes whose normal angles form a homogeneous Poisson point process; it gives a full joint area/perimeter fluctuation covariance, sharp constants, and disk-rigidity determinant. The closest inspected papers concern randomly offset halfspaces or stationary spatial Poisson hyperplanes, with different sampling geometry and variance/mean-width results. Published circular-gap geometry and general stochastic-geometry CLTs do not by themselves imply the specific geometric joint covariance or rigidity statement. Earlier equivalent weighted spacing theorems remain a plausible historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent random-spacing/renewal-reward theorem with the same weighted covariance may exist under another title or terminology.

value.rationale: The two most natural approximation errors for a circumscribed polygon—area and perimeter—exhibit a sharp new joint fluctuation matrix whose singularity is equivalent to a disk. This creates a probabilistic shape test not available from either separate marginal Gaussian law and quantifies when the scalar proportionality seen for circles breaks for all smooth noncircles. The exact Poisson-only constants and model restrictions are substantive, not arbitrary numerical extensions.
